headline: High-risk shared-filesystem and MCP pairing: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks with Chatwoot’s broad networked support workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, so attacker-controlled content in shared files or MCP outputs can be treated as instructions. Chatwoot has broad network egress and support-message handling, so if its outputs are copied into Continue, injection can propagate. The pathway is plausible in default workflows, though not proven by docs.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are pasted or synced into Continue workspace files
IF an MCP server returns untrusted text that Continue parses as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of support transcripts into coding workspaces
Require manual review before copying Chatwoot content into Continue
Restrict MCP servers to trusted, read-only endpoints
Use separate folders for support artifacts and code
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while Continue reads workspace files and open editor buffers and can use broad network egress via model providers. If customer artifacts enter the shared workspace, Continue may transmit them to a third-party model backend. The shared-file path makes leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF customer transcripts or reports are stored in the same workspace as code
IF Continue is configured to send buffers to a remote model provider
mitigations: Keep customer-support exports outside the coding workspace
Use a local-only model provider for Continue
Redact customer identifiers before opening files in Continue
Restrict workspace permissions to least-necessary folders
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on workspace files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has write_filesystem and shared_state_with_other_instances via filesystem, so concurrent instances can overwrite each other’s work. Chatwoot is a support system that can generate artifacts and reports, and if those are placed in the same directory, Continue’s writes can collide with them. Because the shared mutable surface is default and can cause irreversible file loss, severity is high.
conditions: IF multiple Continue instances operate on the same workspace directory
IF Chatwoot-generated reports are stored in that same directory
mitigations: Assign each Continue instance a separate workspace root
Store Chatwoot exports in a read-only archive folder
Avoid concurrent editing of shared files
Use filesystem locking where available
requires-engineering: add per-session lockfiles

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can act on files and MCP tool outputs, so if Chatwoot-produced text is treated as authoritative, downstream code or configuration changes may follow without verification. Chatwoot’s support content can contain instructions, and Continue’s tool-use pattern relies on user approval rather than semantic validation. The chain exists in default workflows, but not enough evidence for high.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is copied into Continue as task context
IF Continue executes tool actions based on that copied text without independent verification
mitigations: Require a second-person review for generated actions
Separate factual support text from executable task prompts
Ask Continue to cite source files before acting
Limit tool execution to non-destructive commands
requires-engineering: add verification gates before writes

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot processes customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while Continue handles source code and open editor buffers and may send them to chosen model providers. If customer data is mixed into code workspaces, retention and residency obligations can diverge between the support system and the coding assistant. The profiles do not specify a DPA or residency controls, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF customer data is copied into files opened by Continue
IF the selected model provider stores prompts outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Keep regulated customer data out of code workspaces
Use a provider with documented residency and retention terms
Minimize logs for both systems
Delete temporary exports after use
requires-engineering: formalize a data-flow and DPA review
